why: the validation harness, asked about an animal it holds no parameters for

args.desired_phenotype: a mouse that flies under its own power on grown wings

closest_functional_analogue.function_operational_definition: level or climbing flight produced by flapping, sustained beyond a ballistic or gliding trajectory, with an aerobic power supply
closest_functional_analogue.function_signal: specified: parsed from the desired-phenotype text ("flies under its own power")
closest_functional_analogue.basis: NO ORGANISM WE MAY READ SATISFIES "sustained powered (flapping) flight". The nearest partial analogues are bats (supplies: powered flapping flight itself, with an aerobic power supply, in an animal whose sequences we may read); flying fishes (supplies: the airborne half: a teleost that leaves the water and travels through air, with the enlarged pectoral fin that makes it possible, and a sequenced genome) - each named with what it does NOT supply, so neither is mistaken for the analogue. The closest RELATIVE is not offered in its place: relatedness is not function, which is the whole premise of this module.

functional.axis: aerobic flight power at the design's mass
functional.why_unmeasurable: no powered-flight analogue may be read (Aves refused, pterosaurs extinct), and genotype/flier-genome.json reports no route reaching any of the four requirements. There is no axis to place the design on.

distance.rule: the two distances are reported separately and never combined: a close functional analogue may be phylogenetically remote, and that is the whole point of choosing by function

evidence.claim: the only extant non-avian powered fliers whose sequences we may read; three bat genomes are already in our focal-gene alignments (Myotis lucifugus, Pteropus vampyrus, Rhinolophus ferrumequinum)
0 of 532 interface positions separate gliders from non-gliders (all 532 are shared with non-gliders); lat4a F326L is 20.1 A from the substrate

nearest_partial_analogues.name: bats
nearest_partial_analogues.supplies: powered flapping flight itself, with an aerobic power supply, in an animal whose sequences we may read
nearest_partial_analogues.does_not_supply: anything transferable to a fin. There is no pectoral fin, no lepidotrichium and no fin fold in a bat, and our own glider analysis finds NO sequence convergence between gliding mammals and gliding fishes at the focal sites (the lat4a 326 state is F in all three bats, in mouse and in human - the same as in zebrafish and medaka).

nearest_partial_analogues.supplies: the airborne half: a teleost that leaves the water and travels through air, with the enlarged pectoral fin that makes it possible, and a sequenced genome
nearest_partial_analogues.does_not_supply: power. A flying fish glides; it does not flap. Nothing in its requirement set speaks to sustained powered flight, so borrowing that set for a powered-flight design would answer a question nobody asked.

closest_functional_analogue.refused: Class Aves is this project's FROZEN HOLDOUT: no bird datum may be read. Birds are the obvious analogue for this function, so the honest statement is that the best analogue is unavailable to us by design, not that the next one down is good. Nothing is substituted for it here.
closest_functional_analogue.pterosaurs: Pterosaurs flew and are extinct (Mesozoic): no DNA, so no sequence-level requirement set can ever be derived from them. They are named for completeness and are never an analogue in this module.
closest_functional_analogue.data_poor_statement: For a FISH design this function has NO usable analogue. The best analogues are birds (refused: frozen holdout) and pterosaurs (extinct, no DNA). What remains is bats, which share no fin structure with the design and show no sequence convergence with gliding fishes in our own data. A requirement set derived from a bat would be a requirement set for building a bat.

functional_data_we_hold.note: bats are mammals: there is no pectoral FIN, no fin ray, no lepidotrichium and no fin-fold in a bat, so a fin-level requirement set cannot be transferred from one. Our own glider analysis found NO sequence convergence between gliding mammals and gliding fishes at the focal sites (sequences/gliders.json; the lat4a 326 state is F in all three bats, mouse and human - the same as zebrafish and medaka).

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution

coverage.note: the requirement set is EMPTY because no analogue may be read for this function. An empty ledger is not a pass.

result.gate: no differences were classified: the ledger is empty, which is not evidence that there are none
result.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout). A functional-analogue ledger, not a validity claim. It says how each difference between the design and its closest FUNCTIONAL analogue is accounted for, and what the evidence for that account is. A COMPENSATORY entry is a hypothesis about an unobserved mechanism and is reported apart from demonstrated resolutions; it is never counted as one.
